findings.reason: the node would otherwise implement the fast path as specified, land a review-gate bypass, and fail its own case 3; the plan needs the coverage fact recorded in the contract (or the fast path restricted to requests that still prove a covering review without `review_coverage`).
findings.text: s4's mechanism is "a request whose stored section and contract digests equal the plan's present ones is answered from them, without calling `review_coverage`", but today `_plan_review_owed` uses `review_coverage`'s `uncovered` set to decide that a request whose units no stored review covers is owed the dispatch gate's verdict (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:3305-3332`), and a contract carries only `section`/`section_digest`/`document_digest` (`queue_admission.py:3122-3135`), no record of coverage. An unchanged plan whose covering review was later removed or left incomplete therefore passes the fast path and launches unreviewed, while a fresh dispatch of the same section holds — which is exactly what the section's own done-when, "Each request's verdict equals the verdict of a fresh direct dispatch at the same moment", forbids.

findings.reason: the assertion passes on the unfixed attribution, so the stage-clock half of the node can close with no proof that wait resolution was separated; the case needs a fixture where wait resolution is made to take measurable time and `waits_seconds` is shown to carry it while `launch_seconds` excludes it.
findings.text: s4's fourth case asserts that "its `release_seconds`, `waits_seconds` and `launch_seconds` sum to the pass duration within 0.1 s", but the row carries no per-stage truth to compare against: an implementation that writes `waits_seconds = 0` and lets `launch_seconds` keep the whole `ended - released` span satisfies the sum exactly, which is the state the section exists to remove (wait resolution timed as launch).

findings.reason: the node would deliver a test whose declared control cannot go red, which is the one property the section's gate rests on; stating the second admittable request in the done-when makes the control able to fail.
findings.text: s21's first case asserts "`crew admit --run` launches the named request and no other" with the launcher stubbed, and its negative control is "runs the whole pass for `--run`, and the first case fails"; with a single admittable queued request in the fixture, the whole pass launches that same request and the case still passes, so the named control discriminates nothing unless the fixture also holds a second queued request the lane can admit.
